<div style="text-align: center;">

## **Research Question: Which demographic and time-determined factors predict longer case processing times for Black civilian complaints against NYPD officers?**

</div>



```{r}
# Load required packages
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(knitr)
library(MASS)


allegations <- read.csv("allegations_202007271729.csv")

# Clean and prepare data 

allegations_clean <- subset(as.data.frame(allegations), 
              select = c(year_received, month_received,
         year_closed, month_closed, rank_now, rank_incident, mos_ethnicity, 
         mos_gender, mos_age_incident, 
         complainant_gender, complainant_ethnicity, complainant_age_incident, 
         fado_type))

# remove any rows containing a missing value
allegations_clean <- allegations_clean[complete.cases(allegations_clean),]

# Filter data to only black complainants

allegations_clean2 <- subset(allegations_clean, complainant_ethnicity == "Black")

#approximate the response variable of case process time in terms of months
allegations_clean2 <- allegations_clean2 %>% mutate(
  case_process_time = (year_closed - year_received) * 12 +
      abs(month_closed - month_received))
```

## Preliminary Model


```{r}
#Build the linear regression model
model1 <- lm(case_process_time ~ year_received + rank_now + rank_incident + 
               mos_ethnicity + mos_gender + mos_age_incident + 
         complainant_gender + complainant_age_incident + fado_type + 
           complainant_age_incident:fado_type, data = allegations_clean2)

summary(model1)

```



```{r, fig.height=3, fig.width=6}
# use plots to check the assumptions
y_value <- resid(model1)
x_value <- fitted(model1)

par(mfrow=c(1,2))

# plots the residual vs fitted plot
plot(x = x_value, y = y_value, main="Residual vs Fitted", xlab="Fitted", 
     ylab="Residuals")

# use qqnorm() and qqline() with residuals to display QQ plot
qqnorm(y_value)
qqline(y_value)
```
##Models for quantitative variables

```{r, fig.height=3, fig.width=8}
# use this command to plot these in a single grid
par(mfrow=c(1,3))

# run plots for numerical predictors
plot(x = allegations_clean2$mos_age_incident, y = y_value, main="Residual vs Cop Age at Incident", xlab="Age", ylab="Residual")
plot(x = allegations_clean2$complainant_age_incident, y = y_value, main="Residual vs Complainant Age at Incident", xlab="Age", ylab="Residual")
plot(x = allegations_clean2$year_received, y = y_value, main="Residual vs Year Received", xlab="Year", ylab="Residual")
```

```{r, fig.height=6, fig.width=8}

boxplot(y_value ~ allegations_clean2$rank_incident , main="Residual vs Rank at incident", xlab="Race", ylab="Residuals")
```

##Fixing Model Assumption violations

```{r}
# apply boxCox() on model1

#boxCox(model1)

#powerTransform(model1)


bcCPT <- allegations_clean2$case_process_time^0.4


# do a log transformation to try and fix right skew
logCPT <- log(allegations_clean2$case_process_time)

#Check sqrt tranformation just in case
sqrtCPT <- sqrt(allegations_clean2$case_process_time)

```

```{r, fig.height=3, fig.width=6}
#recheck model with log
modellog <- lm(logCPT ~ year_received + rank_now + rank_incident + 
               mos_ethnicity + mos_gender + mos_age_incident + 
         complainant_gender + complainant_age_incident + fado_type + 
           complainant_age_incident:fado_type, data = allegations_clean2)

summary(modellog)
#Re-Check plots
y_value1 <- resid(modellog)
x_value1 <- fitted(modellog)

par(mfrow=c(1,2))

# plots the residual vs fitted plot
plot(x = x_value1, y = y_value1, main="Residual vs Fitted", xlab="Fitted", 
     ylab="Residuals")

# use qqnorm() and qqline() with residuals to display QQ plot
qqnorm(y_value1)
qqline(y_value1)
```

##Filter out predictors
```{r}
#Use ANOVA to determine if there are any statistically insignificant predictors
anova(modellog)

#Use confint to determine relevance of nueric predictors
modelCI_1 <- confint(modellog, "year_received")
modelCI_6 <- confint(modellog, "mos_age_incident")
modelCI_8 <- confint(modellog, "complainant_age_incident")
```

##Now that we determined that complainant_age_incident and the interaction term may not be significant, lets test to make sure the model is improved or otherwise unchanged by the removal.
```{r}

#New reduced model
modelred <- lm(logCPT ~ year_received + rank_now + rank_incident + 
               mos_ethnicity + mos_gender + mos_age_incident + 
         complainant_gender + fado_type, 
         data = allegations_clean2)
summary(modelred)

#Check if removal was significant using ANOVA
anova(modelred, modellog)
```
